description: Pinned configuration for keel's live-LLM flywheel benchmark suite. Runs are reproducible and comparable over time because models, trial counts, worker parallelism, scenario counts and the Wilson z are all fixed here. The adversarial control (flywheel_adversarial.py) runs standalone: it has three conditions rather than the without/with pair this suite aggregates.

models.temperature: none — opus-4-8 adaptive thinking forces temp=1; sending a temperature returns HTTP 400, so no temperature field is ever sent

key.note: read lazily at call time, cached in-process, never printed or logged

benchmarks.measures: Synthetic flywheel retrieval-lift: 20 scenarios each carrying an arbitrary project convention a competent model cannot guess a priori. Recorded via `keel learn`, retrieved via `keel brief`. Solve WITHOUT vs WITH the retrieved lesson; dual judge scores rule-compliance.

Real-corpus flywheel retrieval-lift: 16 real, documented VS Code conventions attached to their real files (real path + real content) and retrieved via `keel brief`. Answers the 'you invented those conventions' objection to the synthetic run.
benchmarks.requires: keel binary (KEEL_BIN) + a microsoft/vscode checkout (CORPUS_SRC, default ~/keel-vscode-demo)

benchmarks.measures: Real-corpus flywheel retrieval-lift on Django (Python): 12 real, documented django/django conventions attached to their real files and retrieved via `keel brief`. Generalizes the effect beyond TypeScript.
benchmarks.requires: keel binary (KEEL_BIN) + a django/django checkout (CORPUS_SRC, default ~/keel-django-demo)

benchmarks.measures: Real-corpus flywheel retrieval-lift on Prometheus (Go): 12 real, documented prometheus/prometheus conventions attached to their real files and retrieved via `keel brief`. Lowest model prior of the three, so the highest lift.
benchmarks.requires: keel binary (KEEL_BIN) + a prometheus/prometheus checkout (CORPUS_SRC, default ~/keel-go-demo)

benchmarks.measures: Real-corpus flywheel retrieval-lift on Tokio (Rust): 12 real, idiomatic tokio-rs/tokio conventions attached to their real files and retrieved via `keel brief`. Rust is the language keel itself is written in.
benchmarks.requires: keel binary (KEEL_BIN) + a tokio-rs/tokio checkout (CORPUS_SRC, default ~/keel-rust-demo)
